# BLE handshake transcripts v1 (docs/BLE_PROTOCOL.md section 11; docs/ANDROID_BLE_DESIGN.md 3.5).
# Generated by tools/gen_ble_handshake_v1 (Rust; snow =0.10.0 for Noise, RustCrypto hkdf/sha2 for the
# derivations, chacha20poly1305 for frames with the header as AD; every version pinned by Cargo.lock),
# an implementation independent of noise-c. Before writing, the tool reproduced the official Noise
# vectors (XXpsk3 1, IK 2, 0 skipped), its AEAD path against snow, and 66 records of
# ble_session_v1.txt. These are NOT conformance vectors (the official Noise files are run separately).
# Every key, ephemeral, setup code and token is a visibly synthetic TEST value, never a real secret.
#
# One device lifetime, in order: claim_a (phone A claims; the device generates identity D1),
# session_a (A: IK, then INVITE_CREATE), add_b (phone B joins with the invitation token, slot 1),
# session_b, recovery_c (phone C recovers with the recovery armed; the device generates identity D2;
# EV_CONFIRM_ON_DEVICE, three presses, ENROLL_RESULT {0}), session_c (IK with D2). Each transcript
# ends with an encrypted END_SESSION from the phone and its encrypted response. txn: HELLO 1 (not
# recorded: codec vectors), HS message 0 = 2, HS message 2 = 3, then increasing.
#
# Records (bytes "x:<hex>", "-" = empty):
#   hs    one handshake: inputs and derived values. session_id = HELLO session ID (decimal; LE in the
#         prologue); claim_state, hello_flags, device_id_hash = the HELLO response fields; *_ephemeral
#         = ephemeral PRIVATE keys (test-only fixed ephemerals); device_static = the device identity
#         private key in use (generated by the device at claim/recovery); name = XX message 3 name.
#   frame plain HS frames on the wire (header + body); n = order within the transcript.
#   hash  Noise handshake hash after the last handshake message.
#   enc   encrypted frames: nonce = per-direction counter, header = the AD, plain = body plaintext.
#   neg   negative case: base transcript, the changed input, which side fails at which frame (n),
#         and the exact bytes that side receives. device_rejects = the device answers
#         HANDSHAKE_FAILED (plain) and closes; device_drops = it closes without any reply;
#         phone_rejects = the phone's Noise processing fails; phone_aborts = the phone's identity
#         check refuses (before sending message 3).
